newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to build $247 mln lube mineral oil plant.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to build $247 mln lube mineral oil plant.

text.p: Egyptian state banks, insurance and oil firms have agreed to build a lubrication mineral oil plant with an 840 million pounds ($247 million) investment, industry sources said on Thursday.
"The costs are fully covered either through cash flows or credit facilities," a source close to the agreement told Reuters.
The plant, called Alexandria Company for Mineral Oils, will have an initial annual capacity of 100,000 tonnes, they added.
Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi was quoted in newspapers on Thursday as saying the project was aimed at reducing Egypt's imports of the product, used for vehicles and industrial engines.

Some 420 million pounds will be available in cash from the shareholders, the sources said. National Bank of Egypt and Banque Misr will each hold 20 percent and state-owned Alexandria Petroleum holds 15 percent.
The firm will represent shareholders and operate the new project at its plant in Alexandria, the sources said.
